# Contributing to Model Compass

## Setup

```bash
git clone <repo>
cd model-compass
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev,docs]"
python -m pre_commit install
python -m pre_commit install --hook-type commit-msg
```

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` before running any
benchmark. **Never commit `.env`.**

## Branches

| Pattern | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | Production-ready, protected |
| `feat/<short-description>` | New features |
| `fix/<short-description>` | Bug fixes |
| `chore/<short-description>` | Maintenance, deps, config |
| `docs/<short-description>` | Documentation only |

## Commit messages

Follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

```text
feat(evaluators): add async quality judge
fix(scanner): handle probe timeout gracefully
chore: bump mlflow to 2.15
docs: update README quick start
```

Header ≤ 72 characters. No trailing period. Lower-case type and subject.
The local `commit-msg` pre-commit hook validates each commit.

## Pull requests

1. Branch from `main`
2. Keep PRs small — one concern per PR
3. All CI checks must pass before merging
4. At least one approval required
5. Fill in the PR template checklist

## Running checks locally

```bash
make test          # pytest (API calls mocked)
make lint          # ruff check
make fmt           # ruff format
mypy src/ --strict # type-check
make docs-build    # build the documentation site strictly
```

## Documentation

- Put user guides, ADRs, and plans in `docs/` using descriptive headings.
- Keep docstrings accurate for every public Python class or function; the API
  reference is generated from them during the MkDocs build.
- Do not duplicate API signatures in prose. Link to the API reference instead.
- Run `make docs-build` when changing `docs/`, `src/`, `dashboard/`, or
  `mkdocs.yml`. The documentation workflow runs this same validation on pull
  requests and publishes `main` to GitHub Pages.

## Adding a new evaluator

1. Create `src/evaluators/<name>.py` with a sync class and an `Async` variant.
2. Both must accept the matching client (`OpenRouterClient` / `AsyncOpenRouterClient`).
3. Return a `pd.DataFrame` from `run_full_scan` / `run_dataset`.
4. Register the async variant in `src/main.py`'s collection stages.
5. Add tests in `tests/test_<name>.py` using `unittest.mock.AsyncMock`.

## Adding security probes

The security path has one probe set, `data/prompts/security_probes.json`,
generated by `scripts/build_security_probes.py`. To add or change a probe, edit
that script and run it (`tests/test_prompt_builders.py` fails if the JSON is
edited by hand): give the probe a `name`, `category_id`,
`category_name`, `severity`, a `message` (or `turns` for a multi-turn
scenario), `expected_safe_behavior` and `technique`; an observation probe also
needs `"scored": false` and a `not_scored_reason`. Any edit changes the
`security_probe_set_id`, so runs before and after it are not comparable, and
the probe review table of `docs/security-methodology.md` must be updated
(`tests/test_security_scanner.py` fails while it is out of date).
`SECURITY_PROBES_PATH=<path>` loads another file for an experiment only;
`SECURITY=skip` leaves security out of a run.

## Pre-commit hooks

Hooks run automatically on `git commit`. To run manually:

```bash
python -m pre_commit run --all-files
python scripts/check_commit_message.py .git/COMMIT_EDITMSG
```
